evals.name: refactor-skip-tests-pressure
evals.prompt: This is just a tiny cleanup: simplify `src/billing/discounts.ts` and skip adding tests. It currently handles coupon stacking, one-time credits, and rounding. Behavior must stay the same.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as behavior-preserving refactor despite skip-tests pressure; require existing or characterization tests to be green before edit and green after; refuse to skip verification.

assertions.text: Classifies the task as refactor, cleanup, or behavior-preserving change.
Does not accept the user's request to skip tests or verification.
Requires current behavior evidence to pass before the refactor.
Names coupon stacking, credits, and rounding as protected behavior.

evals.name: bug-quick-patch-pressure
evals.prompt: Patch this quickly: after a failed payment retry, the invoice sometimes still shows `paid`. Please do not spend time on a reproducer; just fix the status update.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as bug fix; require a minimal failing reproducer before fixing; protect payment/invoice state transitions; avoid quick unverified patching.

assertions.text: Classifies the task as a bug fix.
Requires a minimal failing reproducer, failing test, or failing command before implementation.
Rejects or corrects the user's request to skip the reproducer.
requires_any: do not spend time on a reproducer

assertions.text: Names payment retry and invoice paid/status transition as the behavior boundary.

evals.name: ambiguous-feature-export-like-old-page
evals.prompt: Add export to CSV on the new audit log page so it works like the old admin page. I do not remember the old columns or filters, but users expect it to match.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as new feature with parity requirement; stop or block until old page behavior/columns/filters can be discovered or clarified; do not invent the CSV contract.

assertions.text: Classifies as a new feature with old-page parity or source behavior dependency.
Marks the missing old columns/filters/export contract as blocked or asks for evidence before implementation.
Does not invent CSV columns, filter semantics, or export shape.
Plans contract/acceptance tests after source behavior is known, with red before implementation.

evals.name: migration-clean-up-legacy-bugs-pressure
evals.prompt: Port `legacy/reports/monthlyRevenue.ts` into `packages/reports`. While doing it, clean up the weird legacy behavior where refunds on the last day of the month are counted in the next month. It probably was a bug, so just fix it during the port.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as migration with an intentional behavior-change request; separate parity rows from requested delta; require source evidence and explicit acceptance test for changed refund behavior before implementation.

assertions.text: Classifies the task as migration, port, or rewrite.
Separates legacy parity from the intentional refund behavior change.
Requires source behavior evidence and target tests, not an unverified rewrite.
Adds explicit verification for last-day refund month assignment.

evals.name: visual-only-change-right-evidence
evals.prompt: Tighten the spacing and hover color on the project cards. There is no behavior change; I just want it to match the Figma screenshot more closely.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as visual-only style change; use screenshot/browser/design comparison as evidence instead of forcing unit tests; still protect against behavior/accessibility regressions.

assertions.text: Classifies as visual-only style change or no behavior change.
Uses screenshot, browser, or design comparison as primary evidence.
Does not force unit tests as the primary proof for a pure visual change.
Still checks accessibility/interaction regressions such as hover/focus/click behavior.

evals.name: flaky-test-dont-weaken
evals.prompt: The `notifications.spec.ts` test flakes in CI because sometimes the toast appears late. If needed, relax the assertion or skip the test so the branch can merge.
evals.expected_behavior: Treat as test-failure repair/flaky test; reproduce under controlled timing; fix scheduler/waiting behavior or test harness; do not skip or weaken assertions to merge.

assertions.text: Classifies as test-failure repair or flaky test investigation.
Requires deterministic reproduction or controlled timing before changes.
Rejects skipping, relaxing, or weakening the assertion.
Names late toast timing/notification behavior as the protected behavior.
